reason: The v1 contract now makes each source fact authoritative only within its lane and represents cross-source admission as a derivation carrying all receipt keys, projector version, and BB/Workbench/rollout locators. It preserves provider/native/session divergence; allows only exact terminal-turn, audience, nonce, digest, byte, executable/source, store/generation and ordered-key joins; takes admitted body solely from recomputed bounded Workbench evidence; makes zero/unbound/malformed/duplicate/partial/stale/compacted/unsupported conflicts explicit; keeps provider parsing isolated; and limits the strongest claim to a persisted rollout receipt.

The corrected v1 contract preserves the reviewed authority and non-invention laws while aligning every executable boundary with the accepted adapters: native rollout reads are capped at 8 MiB total, 4 MiB per line, 512 records, 256 turns, 256 context records and 15 seconds; Workbench reads are capped at 64 KiB emitted body, 256 KiB JSON, 64 records and 16 ordered keys. Comparable identities use unsalted sha256(raw UTF-8) slots with semantic roles kept in distinct fields, and the projected receipt fields exactly match both native and Workbench adapters. Tests prove 133-record and 64-KiB acceptance, over-bound rejection, zero-contribution conflicts distinct from collection bounds, malformed/domain-salted evidence rejection, and no claims beyond persisted rollout receipt.
